title: Hands off the sash
text: The commercial team wants a new away guernsey with the red sash thinned to a stripe. The members have caught wind of it and the phones are running hot.

choices.label: Keep the sash bold

effects.why: The members and old players kept their sash

choices.result: The sash stays. The merchandise lift the commercial team promised goes with the plan.

choices.label: Approve the modern cut

hit.why: The members feel the sash was sold off

effects.hit_result: The members' backlash runs for weeks.

choices.result: The new jumper sells. The old players are on talkback about it.

title: Collingwood at a full MCG
text: The biggest home-and-away crowd of the year is coming. The group can feel the occasion, and some of the young players have never run out in front of a crowd like it.

choices.label: Lean into the occasion
choices.result: You let them soak it in. A few of the kids look wide-eyed in the warm-up.

choices.label: Treat it as any other week

effects.why: The group kept calm heads in a big week

choices.result: A normal week. Training is a bit flat.

title: The Indigenous players lead the week
text: The club is holding a week to celebrate its Indigenous players and their culture, one of its proudest traditions. The Indigenous players have been asked to lead the program.

choices.label: Give them the week to lead it

effects.why: The Indigenous players led the club's week

choices.result: The players run the week their way. Less time on the track.

choices.label: Football first, ceremony on game night

effects.hit_result: The Indigenous players feel their week was squeezed.

choices.result: A full training week. The ceremony happens on the night.

title: Carlton week
text: Bombers and Blues, one of the oldest grudges in the game. The players want a full-contact session to get the edge back; the physios want a light week.

choices.label: Go full contact

effects.why: The group got its edge back together

effects.hit_result: The bash-and-crash week left the legs heavy.

choices.result: A willing session. A few players come out of it sore.

choices.label: Keep it a light week
choices.result: A light week. The group wanted to bash into it.

title: Chasing the premiership record
text: The press want to know if the club is chasing the outright record for premierships. The answer will be on the back page tomorrow.

choices.label: Say we want the record

effects.why: You said the club wants the record

effects.hit_result: The board now judges the season against your words, and it falls short.

choices.result: It's the back page. Expectations go up a notch.

choices.label: Say one flag at a time

effects.why: The supporters wanted the coach to say it

choices.result: A calm answer. The supporters wanted fire.

title: The finals drought
text: Every September story about the club starts with how long it has been since a finals win. The group has been asked about it all week.

choices.label: Ban talk of it in the rooms

effects.why: The group stayed on the task

choices.result: Nobody mentions it. The press call it a sore point.

choices.label: Own it publicly
choices.result: You talk about it openly. The group feels freer, and a loss would hurt twice.

choices.label: Bring a premiership player in to speak
choices.result: He tells them what September felt like. The past becomes the week's story.

title: Money for Windy Hill
text: The council and the local clubs want Essendon to help pay for a new grandstand and change rooms at Windy Hill. The old guard say it's the club's home; the finance team says the money is needed elsewhere.

choices.label: Put the money in

effects.why: The club looked after its spiritual home

choices.result: The heartland is proud. The finance team is not.

choices.label: Decline politely

effects.why: The local footy community feels forgotten

choices.result: The money stays in football. The locals notice.

title: The local league asks a favour
text: The local district league wants senior players at junior clinics across the north-west on the Monday after a big game. It's the club's heartland and the next generation of members.

choices.label: Send the whole senior list

effects.hit_result: No recovery day, and it showed on the weekend.

choices.result: Every ground in the north-west has a Bomber on it.

choices.label: Send the rookies and one leader

hit.why: The local press noticed none of the stars came

effects.hit_result: The local paper asks where the stars were.

choices.result: The rookies love it. The kids wanted the stars.

choices.label: Say no this week
choices.result: A full recovery day. The local league is disappointed.

title: Questions about the fitness program
text: A new high-performance consultant wants to run an aggressive recovery and supplements program. The club doctor wants every substance signed off in writing before it starts.

choices.label: Back the doctor, slower rollout

effects.why: Every substance was signed off by the doctor

choices.result: The doctor signs off on a cut-down program. The consultant walks.

choices.label: Let the consultant run it

effects.hit_result: The league opens an integrity investigation into the program.

choices.result: The players are fitter than they've ever been.

choices.label: Scrap the program
choices.result: Nothing to answer for. The players wanted it.

title: "Ask them what's in the drink bottles"
text: An opposition coach has hinted on radio that the club cuts corners with its fitness program, and a rival banner ran with it. The group are being asked about it in the press.

choices.label: Front it calmly
choices.result: You answer every question. The story runs another day.

choices.label: Use it as fuel

effects.hit_result: The league doesn't like the tone of the reply.

choices.result: The quote is on the wall in the rooms.

title: The Baby Bombers
text: The press have started calling your young brigade the Baby Bombers. The senior players are watching where their games go.

choices.label: Play the kids together

effects.why: The senior players lost games to the kids

choices.result: Five kids in the side. A few old heads sit in the stands.

choices.label: Bring them through one at a time

effects.why: Games are earned, not handed out

choices.result: A steady side. Two of the kids are getting restless.

title: A gala dinner for cancer research
text: The club is playing a match to raise money for cancer research, and the committee wants the players at a gala dinner midweek. It's a personal cause for several staff.

choices.label: Send the whole group

effects.why: The whole group turned up for the staff's cause

effects.hit_result: The late night showed on the weekend.

choices.result: A full room and a big night for the cause.

choices.label: Send the leaders only

effects.hit_result: The committee notices the empty tables.

choices.result: The leaders go. The rest of the group stays home and rests.

title: Gently in manner, resolutely in deed
text: A scuffle broke out at training. The leadership group want to read the club motto at the next meeting and make an example of it, and the player involved is popular.

choices.label: Make an example of it

effects.why: The leaders held the group to the motto

choices.result: The motto is read out and the incident is named. The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Deal with it privately

effects.hit_result: The leaders feel you went around them.

choices.result: A quiet word behind closed doors. The meeting moves on.

title: Chasing a members' record
text: The club is chasing a membership record, and marketing want the coach in a campaign video and a run of member events through the season.

choices.label: Front the campaign yourself
choices.result: Your face is on every tram. Less time with the list.

choices.label: Let the players front it
choices.result: The players do the events. It eats into their week.

choices.label: Keep out of it
choices.result: Football first. Marketing goes to the board.

title: Talk of a board spill
text: A group of former players and big members are agitating for a board spill. The president has asked you to say publicly that you back the current board.

choices.label: Back the board publicly

effects.hit_result: The old players go on radio against you, and the group hears it.

choices.result: You stand with the president.

choices.label: Stay neutral

effects.why: You kept the coach out of club politics

choices.result: You say it's for the members. The president feels let down.

title: A big fish in the trade period
text: A star from another club wants a big Melbourne club and a big stage. His manager says the price is your first-round pick and a top-dollar contract.

choices.label: Pay it

effects.why: Your out-of-contract players saw the money go to him

choices.result: He arrives to a press pack. The pick and the cap room are gone.

choices.label: Hold the pick

effects.why: The club backed a kid it can build around

choices.result: You keep the pick. The supporters wanted a splash.

title: A premiership legend wants a role
text: A premiership legend has offered to come back as a part-time development coach. The members love the idea; your assistants are wary.

choices.label: Bring him in

effects.hit_result: He and your assistants clash, and the young players get mixed messages.

choices.result: The legend is on the track two days a week.

choices.label: Thank him and decline

effects.why: The chain of command stayed clear

choices.result: He takes it well. The press call it a snub.

title: A coach in waiting
text: The board want to name your senior assistant as your successor now, with a handover at the end of next season. You'd stay in charge until then.

choices.label: Accept the plan

effects.hit_result: Some players start looking past you to the next coach.

choices.result: The handover is announced. The board likes the stability.

choices.label: Refuse and back yourself

effects.why: You kept your authority

effects.hit_result: Your senior assistant takes a job elsewhere.

choices.result: You say you're the coach, full stop. The board is put out.

title: A new Mosquito Fleet?
text: The press say your small, quick forwards look like the old Mosquito Fleet. The forwards coach wants a tall target back in the side.

choices.label: Back the small brigade

effects.why: The tall forward feels shut out

choices.result: Pace and pressure up forward. The big man sits out.

choices.label: Bring back the tall target

effects.why: The forward line kept its shape

choices.result: The tall is back. One of the smalls makes way and isn't happy.

title: {name} has outpolled the captain
text: It's the club's best and fairest night. {name} has polled more votes than the captain, and the room knows it.

choices.label: Make the speech about him

effects.why: You made his night about him
A young player's rise was celebrated

effects.hit_result: The captain is hurt, and the senior players notice.

choices.result: {first} gets the whole speech. The room stands for him.

choices.label: Make it about the group

effects.why: The night belonged to the whole group
He wanted the moment

choices.result: A speech about the group. {first} wanted the moment.

title: "Same old Essendon"
text: Rival supporters have dug up the club's old nickname, "same old Essendon", and turned it into a taunt. A talkback host has picked it up.

choices.label: Wear it with pride
choices.result: You remind everyone the name came from the club's own supporters. Lose again and it sticks.

choices.label: Ignore it

effects.why: The group didn't give the taunt any air

effects.hit_result: The noise runs another week.

choices.result: No comment. Talkback moves on, slowly.

title: North want to go after the kids
text: North Melbourne fans have never forgiven Essendon for the old breakaway that left them out of the first league. Their camp says they'll go after your young midfielders this week.

choices.label: Bring in a hard veteran

effects.why: An old head came in to stand up for the kids

choices.result: The veteran is recalled. A young midfielder makes way.

choices.label: Back the kids to stand up

effects.hit_result: The kids stood up, and came out of it battered.

choices.result: The kids stay in. They know what's coming.

title: A line in the sand
text: The last game against Hawthorn turned spiteful, and the league is watching this one. Your leaders want to stand up for each other if it starts again.

choices.label: Tell them to stand up

effects.why: The group stood up for each other

effects.hit_result: It boils over, and the league hands out fines.

choices.result: The group goes in ready for anything.

choices.label: Tell them to walk away

effects.why: The group kept its discipline

choices.result: The group is told to turn the other cheek. Some feel exposed.

title: The banner tore before the run-through
text: The cheer squad's banner tore before the players ran through it, live on TV. The supporters who made it are gutted, and they've asked for the players to visit.

choices.label: Send players to the banner workshop

effects.why: The players thanked the people who make the banner

effects.hit_result: One evening less to recover showed.

choices.result: The players paint with the cheer squad for the night.

choices.label: Send a signed jumper and a thank-you

effects.hit_result: The cheer squad wanted faces, not a jumper.

choices.result: A jumper goes in the post. The players stay on the track.

title: When to fly to Perth
text: Another trip across the Nullarbor to face West Coast. The players want to fly on the morning of the game and stay home with their families; sports science wants a Thursday flight.

choices.label: Fly Thursday
choices.result: Two nights in a Perth hotel. The players with young kids miss home.

choices.label: Fly on game day
choices.result: An early flight and straight to the ground.
